title: Integrating Bash with a Development Workflow knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Integrating Bash with a Development Workflow”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Repository checks” under lesson 195, “Integrating Bash with a Development Workflow”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Integrating Bash with a Development Workflow”?
options: Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Build incrementally, test locally and in CI, and document assumptions and rollback/recovery steps.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
questions.answer_key: Build incrementally, test locally and in CI, and document assumptions and rollback/recovery steps.
questions.explanation: Build incrementally, test locally and in CI, and document assumptions and rollback/recovery steps. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Integrating Bash with a Development Workflow”?
options: Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
